title: Planar scale
blurb: Turn pixels into millimetres on a front-facing or rectified plane.
formula: scale = L_ref / p_ref     L = p × scale
note: Valid on the reference plane only. Raised or recessed features need the off-plane depth correction.

title: Scale uncertainty
blurb: First-order propagation for L = p × L_ref / p_ref with independent errors.
note: Standard uncertainties, small independent errors. Perspective, distortion, and correlated endpoints are not included; k = 2 is a convention, not a guaranteed 95 % interval.

title: Calibration self-check
blurb: Compare a reference rectangle's image proportions with its known proportions before trusting one rectification.
note: If plane tilt does not explain a difference, use one uniform scale off the plane, record both results, and carry the difference as uncertainty.

title: Homography fit
blurb: Fit a planar homography from four or more image-to-plane point pairs and inspect residuals and local scale.
formula: λ [x, y, 1]ᵀ = H [u, v, 1]ᵀ     local scale = ‖∂(x,y)/∂u‖, ‖∂(x,y)/∂v‖

inputs.label: Point pairs, one per line: u v x y (pixels → mm)

note: Pixels map to millimetres on the plane. A fit can match its control points and still be wrong elsewhere: keep an independent check length.

title: Off-plane depth correction
blurb: Correct a size measured at the reference plane's scale for a feature nearer or farther from the camera.
note: Pinhole model, feature parallel to the image plane. Tilted features are foreshortened as well.

title: Camera distance
blurb: Estimate how far a reference was from the camera, from a 35 mm-equivalent focal length.
formula: f_px ≈ f_35 × diag_px / 43.27     Z ≈ f_px × L / l
note: Assumes the original, uncropped frame, a centred principal point, and negligible distortion. Screenshots and crops break these assumptions.

title: Published-label rounding
blurb: How much a rounded dimension on packaging or a datasheet can actually tell you.
formula: a = ½ × 10^(−decimals) unit     u = a / √3   (rectangular, GUM 4.3.7)
note: Rounding only. Manufacturing tolerance is separate, usually larger, and usually unpublished. Converting units adds digits, not knowledge.

title: Circle tessellation
blurb: Segments needed so a polygonal circle stays within an allowed chordal (sagitta) error.
formula: e = R (1 − cos(π/n))     n ≥ π / acos(1 − e/R)
note: Idealised polygon error only: says nothing about the printed hole, slicer, or machine.

title: Clearance coupon planner
blurb: Plan an exploratory hole series around a pin, using diametral differences.
formula: hole D = d + c_diametral     radial = c_diametral / 2
note: Example test settings, not recommended fits. Print with the intended material, orientation, layers and cooling; examples/clearance-coupon.scad makes the part.

title: Coating allowance
blurb: Primer and paint shrink every slot and hole they touch.
note: Test the coupon in its finished state, or reserve the allowance in the parameter register.

title: Spur gear pair
blurb: Nominal pitch diameters, centre distance, and speed ratio for unshifted external spur gears.
formula: d = m z     a = m (z₁ + z₂) / 2     ω₂/ω₁ = −z₁/z₂
note: Does not define tooth profile, backlash, strength, or profile shift. Use a validated gear generator.

title: Import unit detective
blurb: A mesh came in far too big or small? Find the unit mismatch that explains it.
formula: corrected = observed × factor     rank by |log(corrected / expected)|
note: Compare the same extent (for example overall length) in both fields. Bounding-box scaling and wrong references produce mismatches no unit explains.

title: Evidence-class propagation
blurb: A derived value inherits the weakest evidence class among its inputs.
note: Carry the class into tables, guide curves, and reports so a proposal never reads as a measurement.

title: Wind power estimate
blurb: First estimate of power a small rotor extracts at a steady wind speed.
formula: P = ½ ρ A v³ C_p
note: Not a start-up torque formula. Starting must overcome friction, imbalance, and mechanism resistance at rest: build and measure a prototype.
